mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDPC1 (demand) signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:GDPC1 shows sustained quarterly growth above 5% in prior quarter
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth rate in the next quarter is below 2% or 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE below 4.0% in the prior month signals improving labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% in the prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Historical drops below 4.0% correlated with +20d returns
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 4.0% despite the drop, or 20-day returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in quarterly demand (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) by over 5% in the prior month signal robust economic expansion, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO increase by >5% in the prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Concurrent growth in demand and supply often precedes stock gains
failure_condition: Either GDPC1 or INDPRO doesn’t meet threshold, or returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in FEDFUNDS by over 0.5% in the prior month signals monetary easing, compressing discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: regime:late-cycle expansion and FEDFUNDS falls by >0.5% in prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Historical late-cycle FED cuts preceded +20d returns
failure_condition: In late-cycle, FEDFUNDS decline doesn’t lead to positive returns, or returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment surge (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 signals strong labor demand, prompting positive S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 in the prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Employment spikes correlated with short-term gains
failure_condition: PAYEMS doesn’t hit threshold or 5-day returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly demand (GDPC1) rises by over 2% and unemployment falls by over 0.1pp in the prior month, their combined effect predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up >2% and UNRATE down >0.1pp in prior month
failure_condition: Either signal doesn’t occur or 60-day returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: In contractionary monetary policy, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) by over 3% in the prior month signals resilient supply chains, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: regime:contractionary monetary policy and INDPRO rises >3% in prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Supply growth in contractionary times boosts stocks
failure_condition: INDPRO doesn’t rise or 5-day returns are negative

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.5% signals deflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to cut rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.5% in the prior month
evidence_refs: fact:Deflationary periods followed by rate cuts and gains
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL doesn’t fall below 2.5% or 60-day returns are negative
